event.title: Todd Blanche Terminates Trump's Anti-Weaponization Fund Ahead of Confirmation Hearing
event.canonical_title: Todd Blanche Terminates Trump's Anti-Weaponization Fund Ahead of Confirmation Hearing
event.summary: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has rescinded the $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund initiated by President Donald Trump. This decision comes as Blanche prepares for his confirmation hearing and follows threats from GOP senators to block his appointment if he did not take action regarding the fund, which was intended to support Trump's political allies.

timeline.title: Blanche Gains GOP Support by Abandoning Controversial Fund
timeline.summary: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has secured support from two Republican senators who previously opposed his nomination. This shift follows his commitment to eliminate a $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization' fund, which was intended for settlements to Trump allies, including those involved in the January 6 events.
key_facts: Todd Blanche is the acting Attorney General.
He reached a deal with two GOP senators to gain their support.
The deal involves scrapping a $1.8 billion fund related to Trump allies.

related_events.title: Trump's Settlement Fund Threat Complicates Attorney General Confirmation Talks
related_events.summary: Trump has threatened to advance a proposed $1.8 billion settlement fund if Senate Republicans do not confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general. This statement, made via Truth Social, has introduced new uncertainty into the ongoing discussions regarding Blanche's confirmation, particularly involving Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis.
